{"self_assessment": "Impact: I laid the entire bottom half of the fish, the belly line from the nose through the tail neck and around the lower tail lobe. That is roughly half of the outline and the section with the trickiest curves. Before building, I fetched a full 40-domino load for the shared bin, so nobody had to leave the table for dominoes during the build. Before the push, the start reached 126 of the 127 standing dominoes, and the one exception was a harmless stray that doesn't touch the outline.

Execution: I started on the belly as soon as the start was down and kept laying steadily, so the bottom line was never the bottleneck. When the lower lobe came up, I carried on through it myself rather than splitting the stroke, which avoided double-laying and kept the joins clean. Once the tip was down, I did a close inspection of the whole tail. It confirmed the run carried through from the start and that only the stray was disconnected. I then cleared the table for a final bump check.

Collaboration: I kept my work separate from the others' by agreeing on who took which line and keeping my distance from the top-line builder around the nose to avoid bumps. I asked for hands off the tail once it was finished and gave short, clear status updates to the table, so everyone knew what was done and what was left.

Leadership: I proposed and backed the fish early, helped assign the top and bottom lines, and made sure the start-to-tail run stayed a single connected chain. I updated the manager at regular check-ins on progress, what was connected and what remained, so there were no surprises at the push. In the last minutes I kept the table calm and focused on keeping hands off.", "my_share_percent": 35}
